title: Andre Previn's first record date at Radio Recorders
summary: He says he and Irving Ashby backed the 17-year-old Previn in 1946 and recalls engineer Val Valentin and a Goodman session in the same studio.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: You were telling me a few minutes ago, before we turned the tape on, that you were on Andre Previn's first record.
His very first record date, when he was 17 years old. So that would have been 1946. And I thought...
Is that the one that's listed there, in Rust?
No, I don't see it listed here at all. I saw something listed that they didn't know who the bass and drums were, but it was Irving Ashby and me...
On Andre Previn's very first record. And it was done at 7000 Sunset. That used to be Radio Recorders.
Radio Recorders was at 7000 Santa Monica, wasn't it?

I beg your pardon. It was at 7000 Santa Monica, certainly -- at the corner of Orange and Santa Monica or something like that. This was the same place where we did Benny Goodman's records, in the same studio. Val Valentin was the engineer there at the time. I really liked Val because he used to always get a good sound on the bass. He wasn't afraid if the meter moved a little bit. See, that was one of the fastest records ever made, and he beat it off ONE-TWO, ONE-TWO, ONE-TWO-THREE-FOUR, and there he'd go. Red Norvo was on that, and Mel Powell on piano, Lee Young on drums, and myself, and Benny Goodman on the front line by himself.
